page: Amazon Web Services r8id.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. The system features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for deep learning operations. The server is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

Local storage consists of 11400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 75 Gbps. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Passmark CPU tests, including encryption and physics simulations. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both small and large blocks also rank in the top tier, though the Passmark memory score falls within the average range. Single-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench tests is rated as average to strong.

The server is configured for memory-intensive and high-throughput database workloads, supported by top-tier results in Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations, which reached 240.29 million operations per second. It also achieves top-tier throughput for static web serving and medium-model LLM inference. The high density of DDR5 memory and local NVMe storage provides qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale in-memory databases, data warehousing, and heavy multi-threaded compilation tasks, though the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for primary deep learning training workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services r8id.metal-48xl is a memory-optimized bare-metal server featuring 192 vCPUs across 96 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores running at 3.9 GHz. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory and 11400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The server delivers top-tier performance in multi-core processing, large-block memory bandwidth, and database operations, as evidenced by its 240.29 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. While single-core performance and Passmark memory scores are average to strong, its massive memory capacity, high-speed local storage, and 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth make it highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads. This hardware profile is optimized for large-scale databases, in-memory analytics, multi-threaded software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
